Two different mechanisms decide what happens to people after a state, and a model needs the right one. In a **split on entry**, the outcome is decided when people enter the state: here, 10% of infectious people will go to hospital and the rest will recover, each after their infectious period. With **competing hazards**, two transitions out of a state run at the same time and whichever happens first wins: here, people in hospital are discharged after 10 days on average, but die at a rate of 0.02 per day while they are there, so the share who die depends on both rates. This page puts both in one model, a respiratory infection with hospitalization, and checks the share who die.

## The model

| Parameter | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| β | 0.3 per day | Rate of infection |
| Infectious period | 8 days | Mean time in I (exponential), before recovery or hospitalization |
| Hospitalized | 10% | Share of infectious people who go to hospital, decided on entry to I |
| Stay in hospital | 10 days | Mean time to discharge |
| Death in hospital | 0.02 per day | Rate of death while in hospital, competing with discharge |
| R0 | 2.4 | β × the infectious period |
| Population | 100,000 | |

```{python}
import starsim as ss

S, I, R, H, D = ss.states('S I R H D')
infection = S >> I @ 0.3*I
course    = ss.Transition(I, [R, H], dur=ss.days(8), p=[None, 0.1])  # Split on entry: 10% to H, the rest to R
discharge = H >> R @ ss.days(10)                                     # Competing hazards: discharge ...
death     = H >> D @ ss.perday(0.02)                                 # ... and death
covid = ss.Disease(infection, course, discharge, death, init=dict(I=0.001), name='covid')
```

In `p=[None, 0.1]`, `None` stands for the rest (here, 90%). The diagram, from `diagram()`:

```{python}
covid.diagram()
```

And the equations, in which the split appears as the shares (1 - 0.1) and 0.1 of the flow out of I, and the competing hazards as two flows out of H:

```{python}
covid.equations()
```

A rate given as a number is named by its transition, so the rate of death appears as a parameter called `rate_death`, and a duration by the state it is the time in (`dur_I` and `dur_H`). To give it a name of your own, write it as `ss.par(ss.perday(0.02), name='mu')` (see [Parameters](../user_guide/building_parameters.qmd)).

## Result

```{python}
sim = ss.Sim(covid, total_pop=100_000, stop=ss.days(200))
sim.run()
sim.plot('covid')
```

Of the people admitted to hospital, the share who die is the rate of death over the sum of the two rates out of H: 0.02 / (0.02 + 1/10) = 1/6. The flow `course.H` is the number admitted to hospital:

```{python}
admitted = sim.results.covid['course.H'].sum()
deaths = sim.results.covid.death.sum()
print('Admitted:', round(admitted), 'Died:', round(deaths), 'Share:', round(deaths/admitted, 3))
```
